title: CLO 2024.2 New Features Express: More Powerful Simulation Functions to Upgrade the Precision of Your Designs
description:
Upgrade to CLO 2024.2 and take your design refinement to the next level—the new version is officially launched!  
CLO technical experts will introduce the four main features of the new version from the perspective of the entire garment development process—GPU simulation, accessory simulation, virtual model bust adjustment, the new library window, as well as other updated and enhanced functions.  
What are you waiting for? Explore the new version with CLO now!
transcript:
Hi, everyone!  
Cloud 2024.2 has been officially released!  
Come and check out this new feature!  
Updating your Cloud!  
Upgrading with us!  
New features such as GPU simulation, secondary modeling, and virtual model chest adjustment  
will be fully enhanced with the brand-new Doku window!  
This video will demonstrate the entire process of clothing development,  
helping you connect to new application scenarios.  
Let's take a look at the features you’ve been looking forward to!  

First, the update related to the user interface.  
The Cloud interface now supports dark and light color themes.  
You can switch between the main menu, settings, user settings, and user interface options.  
Select the light color, restart the software, and switch to light theme mode.  
You can now set it according to your preferences.  
Additionally, the UI content displayed in the property editor after selecting the version has been adjusted.  
The material, thinning layer, and shape optimization positions  
have been moved from the bottom to above,  
and a new multi-component layer has been added,  
which will increase the thickness of the rendering and the edge curves.  
A new direction option has been added,  
making it easy to connect with ArrayWare style settings and certain special application scenarios.  

In version 2024.2, we have made major updates to the ArrayWare window.  
The updated ArrayWare is more intuitive and convenient for everyone to access 3D assets.  
First, you can find the new ArrayWare switch button under the original ArrayWare window.  
Click “Try Now” to open the new ArrayWare.  
A new ArrayWare icon will appear in the upper right corner.  
Click the icon to open and close the new ArrayWare window.  
You can also click the button in the lower left corner to return to the old ArrayWare version.  

In the new ArrayWare window, assets are classified into five categories:  
clothing, virtual models, fabrics, accessories, and scenarios.  
Each category includes default CLO assets and community assets from Connect.  
You can choose to download the assets you want or all assets.  
Choose fabrics.  
On the fabric page, select the paper file folder.  
You can also directly click on the paper file folder to enter.  
In the paper file window, the top displays the path for easy navigation and returning to the upper folder.  
When selecting material, you can open the display preview.  
This allows you to see the material more clearly and intuitively.  
You can also display the material as before.  
Switch to clothing, community assets.  
You will see many online 3D clothing assets.  
Here is free content.  
You can download it directly after logging into your Connect account.  
Materials purchased by the account can be viewed, downloaded, and used in the purchase option card on the left.  

Now, you can create a dedicated, multi-selected, custom drawing library.  
Simply click the plus button at the top,  
select the folder you want to add, and create your drawing library.  
You can add multiple different folders to the left side.  
If you need to manage many 3D assets,  
you can create a new custom drawing library for freer management.  

Finally, switch to the second option card at the top.  
After logging into your Closet account, you can browse the files in your current account.  
The section content on the left matches the Closet page,  
making it convenient to quickly find the files you want.  
Then, we will load this shirt with a double click.  
Now, we will use this shirt to show you how to use the Closet app.  
Let’s look at the Closet app.  

First, I will introduce two function optimizations related to blockization.  
When reopening a customized clothing block,  
you can sew it by clicking on the cutout.  
When making clothes,  
it’s usually necessary to sew according to the cutout,  
for example, the bubble sleeve in this style.  
You can see that the cutout on the large sleeve and the sleeve itself is well sewn.  
Now, we define the style of this bubble sleeve as the clothing block.  
This is an automatic blockization labeling tool.  
For this shirt, the current automatic identification is incomplete.  
We can choose to edit the part and redefine the front part of the shirt.  
The back and sleeve parts follow the same process.  
For the collar part that has been accurately identified,  
we can directly save the part quickly.  
After defining it, we can self-define it in the user settings,  
finding the option to sew by clicking on the cutout in the block.  
It is selected by default.  
If you cancel and reload,  
you will see it as a cutout.  
Clicking and reloading the clothing block again,  
you can see it is now sewn by clicking on the cutout.  

Additionally, because parts between styles are usually incompatible,  
to prevent mixing parts from different styles,  
there is a default module combination selection that prevents this.  
Using parts within the same style works normally.  
Switching to other styles triggers a warning window.  
This effectively prevents incorrect part combinations.  

When converting a straight line point to a free curve point,  
you can choose to keep the curve rate or choose a tight conversion.  
Keeping the curve rate creates multiple curve points to maintain the shape,  
the same as before.  
Tight conversion does not create extra points,  
which may change the original curve shape.  
Similarly, when converting a curve point to a straight line point,  
you can choose any method as needed.  
These two modes make conversions more flexible and diverse.  

In the new version,  
we can remove the interlocking relationship between the inner line and the base line on the symmetrical interlocking plate.  
For example, on this shirt,  
we only need to sew a small label on the left side of the large body,  
then remove the interlocking on the inner shape of the right front piece,  
and delete it.  
The base line is handled the same way:  
remove interlocking, select the base line, remove interlocking, then delete the unnecessary base line.  
This long-awaited function will hopefully be useful to everyone in the future.  

Now, I want to change the circle of this shirt to a shoulder strap.  
You can use the plate replacement function.  
This replacement plate feature has also been optimized.  
Right-click on the plate to be replaced,  
then right-click on the replacement plate,  
and select the plate to replace.  
This makes replacement more convenient.  
You can also replace the plate with one that doesn’t match the original.  
After selecting the plate to replace,  
a tool prompt will appear.  
Select the matching point,  
then press Enter to confirm.  
The replacement will complete.  

Next, we will modify the button on the shirt skirt.  
You can modify the button material on the shirt skirt.  
In 2024.2, metal material for buttons has been added to presets.  
Use according to your needs and select the preset you want.  
This makes operation more convenient.  

This time, we have three updates related to sizing codes.  
The new version supports adding sizes based on the current code sizes.  
You can select the smallest size,  
right-click,  
and insert a smaller size at the top.  
Similarly, you can add a new size between two existing sizes.  
The version also adds the function to add a code directly.  
You can enter the code.  
When pasting the code on the board,  
a cross mark will appear in the corresponding position in the 2D window to indicate the code location.  
Switching to the edit code tool,  
you can select the cross mark to enter the code.  
Then, you can switch sizes to simulate and check effects separately.  

Next, two updates about measurement points.  
In 2024.2, the measurement point group function is added.  
You can group measurement points,  
making the measurement information clearer and more flexible.  
Currently, groups are front and back of the costume.  
You can collapse groups you don’t need to see.  
Groups can be classified and renamed based on your preferences.  
When a costume has multiple sizes,  
you can hide sizes you don’t need to see in the measurement point label.  
This makes it easier to focus on the current size.  
You can click the icon again to show the hidden sizes.  

Next, two updates about arrangement.  
In 2024.2, after selecting the size to arrange,  
you can classify the arrangement by size.  
Switching to the machine code,  
you can clearly distinguish the current machine code and other sizes.  
Additionally, the arrangement of different colors has been simplified.  
Arrangement and color are linked.  
Click the color you want to arrange, then arrange.  
Switching to color view shows that the same fabric colors are arranged together.  

From 2024.2, you can adjust the chest shape of the virtual model.  
In the virtual model editor, a new chest editor is added,  
allowing you to create a custom chest model.  
You can adjust the shape to make the chest closer to round or flat-bottomed.  
To reset adjustments, click the reset button in the upper right corner.  
If the shoulder points toward the female model,  
the chest becomes bigger and wider.  
Shorter shoulders mean bigger chest, wider chest means wider chest,  
and higher breast point position corresponds to the female model.  
This parameter can be objectively adjusted and viewed.  

Next, virtual model joints.  
In 2024.2, support for resizing and hiding joints is added.  
Open the virtual model joint editor.  
In the upper right adjustment window, size adjustment is added.  
You can resize joints to your preference or reset to default size.  
If you don’t want to see certain joints, hide them in the right-click menu.  
Right-click again to show them.  
The current joint adjustment window is different from before.  
You can switch between FK and IK modes in the mode area to show corresponding editing tools.  

In 2024.2, the “flatten as a sheet” function is optimized.  
This function extracts chest sheets drawn with a 3D drawing pen.  
Using “flatten as a sheet,”  
the front and back sheet logic opens in the 2D window.  
Line direction presentation is more reasonable.  
After producing the chest sheet,  
during shoulder strap simulation and adjustment, shoulder strap slip often occurs.  
Now, a fixing pin can be added on one side of the shoulder strap.  
You can copy the fixing pin position to the corresponding sheet position  
to facilitate shoulder strap adjustment.  

In 2024.2, the stretch bar extension function is optimized.  
Use the stretch bar tool to add stretch bars.  
Different stretch areas are distinguished by different colors,  
with arrows indicating only the start and end of the stretch bar.  
The attribute editor now includes extension settings for the start and end of the stretch bar.  
You can set different extension effects here to adjust where they end.  
Setting endpoints for two stretch bars on the stretch bar shows that the two bars do not overlap but connect.  

Next, fabric generator function update.  
After opening the fabric generator,  
the upper fabric preview window is blank because no fabric is generated yet.  
After entering information,  
select fabric type, then ingredient.  
Ingredients can be freely selected,  
and ingredient types change according to fabric type.  
This makes fabric ingredient settings more diverse and flexible.  
After selecting ingredients, fabric preview appears on top.  
After setting ingredient ratios, add a prepared texture sticker and apply fabric.  
In the new version, color settings move to the top where material content rests,  
based on user choice and setting.  
Use this new function to replace fabric colors when needed.  

Next, differences from the previous color version.  
There are three braids:  
the leftmost is original,  
the second shows blocking color effect,  
the third shows color replacement effect.  
When blocking color and applying new color,  
texture color on fabric is completely blocked,  
and texture detail becomes lighter.  
Using the new function to replace color:  
select fabric, find it in the attribute editor,  
refresh color, replace,  
and select needed color to complete texture color replacement.  
Replacement color is clearer and retains original texture details compared to fill color.  
This function improves the experience of changing clothing colors.  

When multiple 3D clothing records exist in a file,  
it’s easy to confuse them.  
This update adjusts the shrinkage of 3D clothing records.  
Hovering over a record shows a larger, clearer preview.  
This helps find the desired record among many.  

Next, using this handbag to demonstrate following functions.  
The current handbag material type is wool.  
A new option below—line difference—quickly achieves desired line performance.  
Turning on irregularity randomizes fabric position.  
Slide or enter values to adjust irregularity ratio or frequency for different line effects.  
Enabling the “ball” increases fabric ball effects.  
Slide or enter values to adjust length, thickness, and frequency of fabric balls for more realistic and diverse line performance.  

Additionally, CLOU added a new hair vinegar generator.  
You can conveniently adjust hair length and curve.  
Without much effort, you can easily show the hair vinegar effect.  
Let’s add a new color to the handbag.  
Select all properties,  
change material type to hair,  
and delete texture.  
Open texture and check hair effect.  
Click fabric,  
a new hair vinegar button appears.  
Open hair vinegar generator; default length and curve direction show.  
Click apply and enable rendering.  
Hair effect differs from before.  
Apply a preset hair material.  
Turn on rendering to check effect.  
Open hair vinegar generator.  
Adjust parameters to reduce effect in length picture.  
Switch to curve direction.  
After adjusting, click apply and enable rendering.  
Current effect differs from before.  
Hair vinegar generator length picture also includes cut picture.  
Insert picture, click apply, enable rendering.  
Hair looks like a flower on the cut picture.  
We also provide 15 common hair materials with hair vinegar effect.  
Details on the hair vinegar generator will be explained in a later video—stay tuned.  

Next, adding a new color to the handbag.  
Clicking default add method causes mouseover when material, all properties, and linkage are close,  
and a frame appears explaining added color properties of material and linkage.  
In the new version, you can drag material directly from the handbag window,  
object window, or local folder into the color editor window for easier color changes.  
Now, dragging material from handbag window and releasing on target material info frame changes the color.  
For materials in the object window,  
dragging the added material to 3D clothing shows a link applying to color.  
You can specify default application method: apply only to current color or all colors,  
and choose material or linkage.  
After setting and clicking OK, this window won’t appear again.  
When dragging material from object window to 3D clothing,  
a prompt icon appears on the mouse.  
Use the Control key to switch color application and quickly select the desired color effect.  

In the new color version, you can also hide multiple stickers.  
First, add a sticker to the handbag,  
adjust its Z-axis distance to show the sticker.  
In the new Z-axis distance,  
use Control key to select sticker colors not to hide.  
Right-click to hide other stickers;  
stickers other than the selected colors will be hidden.  

Next, open the shirt group file already wearing the handbag,  
adjust model information display to grid surface.  
Click model to adjust grid level.  
Higher level means more grid,  
smoother skin,  
better display effect for tight clothing.  

In 2024.2, GPU simulation conflict processing is improved.  
CPU and GPU can be switched in simulation mode.  
Choose the common mode for demonstration.  
Add a chest coat to match clothing.  
Opening simulation shows GPU conflict processing is very good.  
Rotate to different angles to see results.  
Generally, GPU simulation is faster than CPU simulation.  
Left and right windows show GPU and CPU simulation respectively.  
Apply a pose to the suit.  
You can see both simulations run faster.  

Finally, the window ring design changes.  
In 2024.2, more stable and portable copy simulation is achieved.  
Right-click button to close the loop,  
you see added copy simulation.  
Open simulation, use hand to capture the copy.  
You can see interaction between copy and template.  
The copy won't easily penetrate the template.  
Simulation is more stable.  

Finally, we render this whole outfit.  
Open rendering window, picture/video properties, switch to all colors in color selection,  
and save a column at the bottom to add a new one.  
In the final rendering, you get a single image showing multiple colors and all colors.  

After 3D design is complete, upload the file to Closet.  
Closet released two main functions this season.  
One is the new content paragraph management tool, allowing detailed recording of clothing information.  
Enter content page, click left arrow to display detailed info.  
Fill every paragraph here.  
Customize paragraphs based on file type, such as Closet project, fabric, etc.  
Using this tool, you can share file information more efficiently.  

The other is the new configuration tool.  
Using it, you can regularly edit 3D clothing material properties online.  
On the right side of the 3D viewfinder, click new configuration button.  
You can regularly edit material properties.  
Change colors using Pantone, ColorRow, etc.  
Add text and PBR stickers.  
Adjust text ratio and position with editing tools.  
New color schemes can be downloaded back to Closet for further editing.  
Through this, non-Closet users can participate in design and development and try new color schemes together.  

The main functions of this update are introduced here.  
Which new function impressed you the most?  
In the future, we will further introduce function summary videos with key features.  
Please continue to follow the official account content.  
Welcome to leave your opinions or practical experiences in the comments.  
Closet’s progress depends on your attention and feedback.  
See you next time.

chunks.title: CLO 2024.2 New Features Express: More Powerful Simulation Functions to Upgrade the Precision of Your Designs
chunks.content: # CLO 2024.2 New Features Express: Enhanced Simulation and Design Precision This document details the new features and improvements in CLO 2024.2, focusing on simulation functions, user interface updates, asset management, virtual model customization, sizing enhancements, and fabric generation. It covers technical explanations, procedures, and examples to help users leverage CLO’s upgraded capabilities for precise clothing design. --- ## User Interface Enhancements This section covers the updated CLO interface, including theme options, property editor rearrangements, and new UI elements to improve user customization and workflow. - **Dark and Light Themes**: Users can switch between dark and light color themes via main menu > settings > user interface options. Changing theme requires restarting the software. - **Property Editor Layout**: Material, thinning layer, and shape optimization controls have moved from the bottom to the top of the property editor. - **Multi-Component Layer**: Added to enhance rendering thickness and edge curve definition. - **New Direction Option**: Facilitates integration with ArrayWare style settings and supports specialized application scenarios. --- ## ArrayWare Window Upgrades This section explains the redesigned ArrayWare window for easier 3D asset management and access. - **New ArrayWare Switch**: Accessible under the original ArrayWare window with a “Try Now” button. - **Categorized Assets**: Five categories—clothing, virtual models, fabrics, accessories, and scenarios—contain both default CLO assets and community assets from Connect. - **Asset Browsing and Downloading**: Users can preview materials and download assets after logging into Connect. Purchased materials are accessible via a dedicated purchase option card. - **Custom Drawing Libraries**: Users can create multi-selected, custom drawing libraries by adding multiple folders for better asset management. - **Closet Account Integration**: After logging in, users can browse their Closet files with a sidebar matching the Closet page layout for quick file access. --- ## Blockization and Sewing Improvements Details enhancements to clothing block editing, automatic block labeling, and sewing operations. - **Sew by Clicking Cutout**: When reopening a custom clothing block, users can sew parts by clicking on cutouts, facilitating styles with complex shapes (e.g., bubble sleeves). - **Automatic Blockization Labeling Tool**: Provides initial automatic identification of clothing parts; incomplete identifications can be manually edited. - **User-Defined Sewing Settings**: Option to sew by clicking the cutout is enabled by default and can be toggled in user settings. - **Style-Part Compatibility Module**: Prevents mixing parts from different styles by issuing warnings when mismatched parts are combined, ensuring correct module combinations. --- ## Curve Point Conversion Flexibility Explains new modes for converting points between straight lines and curves to provide more precise pattern control. - **Straight Line to Free Curve**: - *Keep Curve Rate*: Adds multiple curve points to maintain original shape. - *Tight Conversion*: Does not create extra points, which may alter the curve shape. - **Curve to Straight Line**: Users can choose conversion methods as needed, enhancing flexibility in pattern editing. --- ## Symmetrical Interlocking Plate Editing Describes the new ability to remove interlocking relationships on symmetrical plates for refined editing. - Users can unlink inner lines from base lines on symmetrical plates.

chunks.title: CLO 2024.2 New Features Express: More Powerful Simulation Functions to Upgrade the Precision of Your Designs
chunks.content: - **Straight Line to Free Curve**: - *Keep Curve Rate*: Adds multiple curve points to maintain original shape. - *Tight Conversion*: Does not create extra points, which may alter the curve shape. - **Curve to Straight Line**: Users can choose conversion methods as needed, enhancing flexibility in pattern editing. --- ## Symmetrical Interlocking Plate Editing Describes the new ability to remove interlocking relationships on symmetrical plates for refined editing. - Users can unlink inner lines from base lines on symmetrical plates. - Example: Sewing a small label on one side and removing interlocking lines on the opposite side. - Base lines can also be unlinked and deleted as needed. - This function allows more precise control over symmetrical pattern parts. --- ## Plate Replacement Function Optimization Covers improvements to the plate replacement workflow, increasing convenience and flexibility. - Right-click the plate to be replaced, then right-click the replacement plate and select “replace plate.” - Users can replace plates with non-matching originals. - After selecting the replacement plate, users define matching points, then confirm with Enter. - The replacement completes smoothly, streamlining pattern adjustments. --- ## Button Material Presets Highlights the addition of metal button materials to presets for easier button customization. - Users can select from metal button presets to modify shirt skirt buttons. - Presets simplify the material selection process for buttons. --- ## Sizing Code Enhancements Details new features for managing sizing codes more flexibly. - **Insert Smaller Sizes**: Add sizes smaller than the smallest existing size by right-clicking and inserting at the top. - **Add Sizes Between Existing Codes**: Insert sizes between two existing sizes. - **Direct Code Addition**: Enter sizing codes manually. - **Visual Code Indicators**: Cross marks appear in the 2D window to indicate code locations. - **Edit Code Tool**: Select cross marks to edit codes and simulate different sizes separately. --- ## Measurement Point Grouping and Visibility Explains grouping and visibility controls for measurement points to improve clarity. - Measurement points can be grouped (default groups: front and back). - Groups can be collapsed or renamed for better organization. - Users can hide measurement points of sizes not currently needed, focusing on specific sizes. - Hidden sizes can be toggled visible again with a click. --- ## Arrangement and Color Classification Describes updates to arrangement sorting by size and color for production clarity. - Arrangement can be classified by size after selecting the size to arrange. - Machine code view clearly distinguishes current machine code from others. - Color arrangement is linked with fabric colors: selecting a color arranges all items of that color together. - Simplifies sorting for multi-color production. --- ## Virtual Model Chest and Joint Adjustments Details new tools to customize virtual model chest shape and joint visibility. - **Chest Editor**: - Allows custom shaping of the virtual model’s chest (rounder or flatter). - Parameters affect chest size, width, and breast point position. - Reset button available to restore defaults. - **Joint Editor**: - Resize joints or reset to default.

chunks.content: - Color arrangement is linked with fabric colors: selecting a color arranges all items of that color together. - Simplifies sorting for multi-color production. --- ## Virtual Model Chest and Joint Adjustments Details new tools to customize virtual model chest shape and joint visibility. - **Chest Editor**: - Allows custom shaping of the virtual model’s chest (rounder or flatter). - Parameters affect chest size, width, and breast point position. - Reset button available to restore defaults. - **Joint Editor**: - Resize joints or reset to default. - Hide or show specific joints via right-click context menu. - Switch between FK (Forward Kinematics) and IK (Inverse Kinematics) modes for corresponding editing tools. --- ## Flatten as a Sheet Function Optimization Improves the chest sheet extraction and shoulder strap simulation workflow. - Extracts chest sheets drawn with the 3D drawing pen. - Front and back sheet logic opens in the 2D window with improved line direction presentation. - Fixing pins can be added on shoulder straps to prevent slip during simulation. - Fixing pin positions can be copied to corresponding sheets to facilitate adjustments. --- ## Stretch Bar Extension Enhancements Explains new stretch bar extension controls for detailed stretch area customization. - Stretch bars show different colors for different stretch areas. - Arrows indicate only the start and end points. - Attribute editor includes extension settings for start and end, allowing distinct extension effects. - Multiple stretch bars connect without overlap, maintaining seamless stretch behavior. --- ## Fabric Generator Updates Covers improvements to fabric ingredient selection, preview, and color replacement. - Fabric preview window remains blank until ingredients are selected. - Users choose fabric type, then freely select ingredient types according to fabric type. - Fabric preview updates after ingredient selection. - Ingredient ratios can be set before applying textures and fabric. - Color settings relocated to the top of the material content area. - New function allows fabric color replacement while retaining original texture details, improving color change realism. - Color replacement is clearer and preserves texture better than blocking color methods. --- ## 3D Clothing Record Preview Improvements Enhances preview clarity when multiple 3D clothing records exist in a file. - Hovering over clothing records displays a larger, clearer preview. - Facilitates finding the desired record among multiple entries. --- ## Line Difference and Fabric Ball Effects Introduces new fabric effect options to enhance realism in line appearance and fabric texture. - **Line Difference Option**: Adjusts line performance quickly. - **Irregularity**: Randomizes fabric position with adjustable ratio and frequency. - **Ball Effect**: Adds fabric ball effects with adjustable length, thickness, and frequency. - Enables more diverse and realistic fabric surface details. --- ## Hair Vinegar Generator Describes the new hair vinegar generator for hair material effects. - Allows easy adjustment of hair length and curve. - Users select hair material type, delete default texture, then open the hair vinegar generator. - Default length and curve settings can be applied and rendered.
